question: Can ordinary feedforward backpropagation be realized exactly as the equilibrium and discrete trace of a doubled, dissipative physical relaxation derived from an action, and do the proposed dynamics provide a practically or physically distinct credit-assignment mechanism?

key_findings.claim: The doubled-state equilibrium is algebraically equivalent to standard reverse-mode differentiation for a strictly feedforward network.
key_findings.evidence: Stacking activations makes the global weight matrix strictly block-lower-triangular. With mean m=(x+z)/2 and stress s=x-z, equilibrium satisfies m=σ(Wm+β) and (I-W^T D)s=g. Nilpotency makes the inverse a finite Neumann series; δ=Ds then gives the usual layerwise parameter gradient δm^T. Appendix F expands the same recurrence into the standard backpropagation chain.

anchors.section: 3.5-3.7 Mean-stress variables, equilibria, and gradient computation

key_findings.claim: For forward Euler with the special step size Δt=1, the synchronous recurrence recovers exact backpropagation after 2L global iterations in exact arithmetic.
key_findings.evidence: The mean update becomes the usual layer map, so layers freeze successively and all L forward blocks are correct by iteration L. Once D is fixed, the stress update shifts credit one block per iteration through W^T; the remaining transient vanishes after another L iterations. The appendix proves the layer-freezing induction and gives the corresponding algorithm.

anchors.section: 4.1-4.2 Canonical discretization and exact convergence in 2L steps
D Proof of forward layer freezing
E Algorithmic form of the discrete dynamics

key_findings.claim: The relaxation is not generated by stationary action alone: the paper adds Rayleigh dissipation and a sign-asymmetric Lagrange-d'Alembert rule to obtain the first-order flow.
key_findings.evidence: The velocity-free Lagrangian L=(x-z)^T F((x+z)/2)+C yields algebraic stationarity conditions. Equation 7 augments the Euler-Lagrange equations with -∂R/∂x_dot and an opposite sign for z, using R=(||x_dot||²+||z_dot||²)/2, which produces x_dot=+∂L/∂x and z_dot=-∂L/∂z. Appendix A explicitly motivates this open-system construction. Thus the action organizes the dynamics, but dissipation is an indispensable added ingredient.

anchors.section: A.1 Lagrangian mechanics for dissipative systems
A.2-A.3 Non-reciprocal flow and Lagrangian construction

key_findings.claim: The proposed dynamics remove a separately scheduled backward phase but do not remove weight transport or a reverse credit channel.
key_findings.evidence: Both the continuous stress equation and the discrete recurrence explicitly multiply by W^T D. The related-work discussion itself lists weight transport as a remaining biological issue. A physical implementation therefore needs transposed or reciprocally coupled interactions carrying stress from later to earlier blocks even if mean and stress evolve in one nominal relaxation.

key_findings.claim: Finite-time convergence belongs to the unit-step discrete map, not to the continuous relaxation.
key_findings.evidence: The continuous mean equation contains a leaky term, m_dot=σ(Wm+β)-m, whose already-driven layers approach their fixed points exponentially rather than becoming exactly equal at a finite time. Exact layer freezing occurs only after setting the forward-Euler step to one, which cancels the old state. The text's early suggestion that nilpotency implies finite-time convergence for the relaxation dynamics therefore needs this discrete qualification.

key_findings.claim: Appendix F proves a favorable local equilibrium Jacobian, but its stated conclusion of global exponential stability is stronger than the calculation supports.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix evaluates the Jacobian at equilibrium and uses block triangularity to show diagonal eigenvalues -1. That is a local linearization result. Global exponential stability of the nonlinear, nonsmooth empirical system would additionally require global regularity and a bound controlling off-diagonal nonlinear terms; none is supplied. Appendix B makes a parallel stability claim for the inertial extension from its linearized characteristic roots.

anchors.section: F.2 Exponential stability of the equilibrium

key_findings.claim: The CIFAR-10 experiment shows optimization parity and very close relaxed versus autograd gradients under one controlled training run per step size.
key_findings.evidence: A nine-layer, roughly 5M-parameter VGG-style network is trained for 100 epochs at η∈{0.25,0.5,0.75,1}. All four curves reach about 93% test accuracy. Reported directional misalignment is generally around 10^-7 and SNR exceeds 10^6, while η=1 approaches the theoretical 18-iteration floor for L=9.

anchors.section: H.1-H.2 Training stability and gradient norm consistency
H.3-H.5 Alignment, SNR, and layerwise misalignment

key_findings.claim: The headline approximately 10^-7 agreement describes direction in float32, not full gradient equality at that relative precision.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix H plots 1-cosine at roughly 10^-6 to 10^-8 and global directional error near 10^-7, but the gradient-norm ratio differs from one by roughly +0.0001 to -0.0003. The two metrics are compatible but materially different; the evidence supports near-identical directions with relative scale discrepancies around 10^-4.

key_findings.claim: The study does not establish a runtime, memory, energy, or hardware advantage over ordinary backpropagation.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm 1 permits up to 1,000 relaxation iterations per minibatch and each synchronous iteration updates all state blocks. Even the 18 global sweeps at η=1 are not cost-equivalent to one optimized forward layer sweep plus one reverse layer sweep. The paper reports about two GPU hours per η, but gives no autograd wall-clock/FLOP/memory baseline and no analog or neuromorphic implementation; Section 4 explicitly notes that standard passes skip redundant updates.

key_findings.claim: The formal differentiability assumptions are not fully reconciled with the ReLU-and-pooling network used for validation.
key_findings.evidence: The derivation repeatedly uses the diagonal derivative D=diag(σ') and a smooth equilibrium Jacobian. The experiment instead uses ReLU and stride-2 pooling, including nondifferentiable activation points and a non-elementwise operation. Autodiff chooses subgradients in practice, but the exact theorem is not extended to those cases in the paper.

key_findings.claim: The second-order extension preserves the same equilibria but does not establish that inertial transients are useful or globally controlled.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B adds a mass-weighted kinetic term and obtains damped second-order equations. It observes that zero-velocity equilibria reduce to the first-order stationary equations and inspects linearized characteristic roots. There is no numerical comparison, overshoot analysis, convergence-rate bound for the coupled nonlinear system, or training result for this variant.

key_findings.claim: The split-dynamics variant is an approximation, so its reported matching accuracy does not extend the exact-gradient theorem to that implementation.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix G changes variables to separate activation and credit states and explicitly neglects higher-order nonlinear stress terms in a local expansion. The main text says the simplified scheme was tested with identical accuracy, but the appendix supplies no independent numerical table or exact error theorem. Accuracy parity therefore cannot substitute for exact gradient equivalence away from small stress.

method.core_idea: Embed a feedforward computation and its reverse sensitivity into the mean and difference of two coupled state copies, then interpret their dissipative relaxation through a Bateman-Galley-style doubled action.
method.mechanism: A strictly block-lower-triangular global W defines the forward vector field F(m)=σ(Wm+β)-m. The Lagrangian couples the stress x-z to F((x+z)/2) and adds output loss. A Rayleigh-dissipative, sign-asymmetric variational rule gives a mean equation equal to forward relaxation and a stress equation driven by W^T D plus the output loss gradient. At equilibrium, finite nilpotent Neumann sums recover the reverse-mode adjoint. Forward Euler at Δt=1 yields layer-by-layer forward freezing followed by layer-by-layer credit propagation in 2L synchronous iterations.
assumptions: The computation graph is an acyclic, strictly feedforward chain that can be represented by a strictly block-lower-triangular W.
Activation derivatives exist where the trajectory and equilibrium are evaluated, and the chosen subgradient behavior is compatible with the theory.
The physical substrate can implement matched W and W^T couplings and the required sign-asymmetric doubled-state dynamics.
Exact arithmetic underlies the 2L finite-iteration result; finite precision and stopping tolerances only approximate it.
The unit Euler step is numerically admissible; smaller η values sacrifice finite-step exactness for damping.
A squared-error or differentiable output loss supplies the terminal drive g without an additional discrete phase.
Local Jacobian spectra are informative about relaxation near equilibrium even though they do not alone prove global stability.

techniques.role: Stacks all layers into one strictly lower block-triangular map whose finite powers encode feedforward depth.
Uses two copies with opposite variational signs to represent non-reciprocal dissipative flow.
Separates forward activations in the mean from reverse sensitivities in the state difference.
Turns the equilibrium inverse (I-W^T D)^-1 into a finite backpropagation series through nilpotency.
Recovers exact layer freezing and reverse credit propagation after 2L global Euler iterations.
Compares relaxation gradients with symbolic gradients using cosine, norm ratio, SNR, and layerwise error.

limitations: Author-stated: the method retains the weight-transport problem because the stress dynamics use W^T.
Author-stated: conventional digital forward/backward passes are an optimized schedule that avoids the redundant layer updates of a global synchronous relaxation.
Author-stated: a concrete energy-efficient physical implementation and broader links to path integrals, Noether symmetry, and symplectic structure remain future work.
Reviewer-identified: the first-order flow requires Rayleigh dissipation in addition to the action, so 'from the least-action principle' is incomplete if read as stationary action alone.
Reviewer-identified: the global exponential-stability claim exceeds the local equilibrium-Jacobian calculation, especially with ReLU nonsmoothness.
Reviewer-identified: the 2L theorem assumes a feedforward nilpotent graph, exact arithmetic, and the special unit Euler step; the continuous ODE only converges asymptotically.
Reviewer-identified: a single CIFAR-10 architecture, shared random seeds, and no run-to-run intervals cannot establish broad optimization robustness.
Reviewer-identified: no matched latency, FLOP, memory, energy, or hardware comparison supports the physical-efficiency motivation.
Reviewer-identified: the theoretical differentiability and elementwise-activation setup is not formally extended to the empirical ReLU-and-pooling architecture.
Reviewer-identified: the split and second-order variants receive no independent quantitative evaluation sufficient to validate their stronger claims.
failure_modes: A physical device without precise reciprocal W/W^T couplings will accumulate biased credit even if its forward relaxation is accurate.
Finite precision, noisy derivatives, or an η below one destroys exact 2L termination and can amplify early-layer error over many global sweeps.
For deep networks, updating every block during every synchronous iteration can turn the nominal 2L trace into substantially more block work than scheduled backpropagation.
ReLU threshold crossings make D discontinuous, invalidating a smooth local-Jacobian argument and potentially changing stress propagation during relaxation.
Feedback, recurrence, normalization across examples, attention, or skip graphs that are not strictly nilpotent require a different convergence argument.
The inertial extension can overshoot or oscillate under poorly chosen mass and damping even though its equilibrium is unchanged.
The split approximation can depart from exact gradients when stress is not small because discarded nonlinear terms become material.
Using cosine agreement alone can hide scale bias large enough to affect optimization under clipping, weight decay, or adaptive updates.
reusable_insights: A nilpotent global operator provides a clean algebraic bridge between layer depth, forward substitution, and finite reverse-mode Neumann sums.
Mean/difference coordinates can separate inference state from credit state inside a single coupled dynamical system.
When claiming physical learning, audit every transpose, sign convention, damping term, and externally imposed terminal drive rather than only the action functional.
Distinguish finite-step properties of a special discretization from convergence properties of its parent continuous-time ODE.
Report gradient direction, norm, task effect, and computational cost together; any one metric can mask a consequential mismatch.
Compare synchronous global iterations in block-update or FLOP units before treating their count as comparable to scheduled layer sweeps.
open_questions: Can an actual analog or neuromorphic substrate implement the required transpose coupling more efficiently than a digital reverse pass?
Is there a genuinely local adaptation rule that learns the reverse coupling without exact weight transport while preserving the equilibrium-gradient theorem?
What global regularity conditions would turn the local triangular Jacobian result into a rigorous global convergence theorem?
Can the construction extend exactly to residual, recurrent, attention, normalization, and shared-parameter graphs that are not simple nilpotent chains?
How do device noise, quantization, derivative mismatch, and asynchronous updates alter gradient bias with depth?
Does the second-order system offer a measured convergence or energy benefit after controlling overshoot and total physical time?
Can the split dynamics receive an error bound in stress magnitude and a direct gradient-fidelity evaluation?

competitive_landscape.title: Equilibrium Propagation: Bridging the Gap Between Energy-Based Models and Backpropagation
competitive_landscape.difference: Equilibrium Propagation estimates gradients from free and weakly nudged equilibria of a scalar energy model and naturally assumes symmetric interactions. The present paper instead doubles a non-conservative feedforward state and recovers the exact reverse-mode gradient at one equilibrium/discrete trace, but it still explicitly requires W^T coupling.

competitive_landscape.title: Dual Propagation: Accelerating Contrastive Hebbian Learning with Dyadic Neurons
competitive_landscape.difference: Dual Propagation already uses paired neuronal quantities to combine inference and teaching and reports large-scale empirical acceleration. The target's narrower addition is a Bateman-Galley-style action plus an exact 2L feedforward trace; it does not establish a better compute or hardware result than the dyadic approach.

competitive_landscape.title: Predictive Coding Can Do Exact Backpropagation on Convolutional and Recurrent Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Song et al. show that a predictive-coding inference procedure can reproduce exact backpropagation on convolutional and recurrent networks under suitable initialization and scheduling. The present result is therefore not the first exact relaxation-to-BP equivalence; its distinctive claim is the doubled variational mechanics and nilpotent 2L synchronous trace for feedforward graphs.

competitive_landscape.title: Equilibrium Propagation for Non-Conservative Systems
competitive_landscape.difference: This concurrent work, including the target author, augments arbitrary non-conservative systems so equilibrium propagation can obtain exact gradients without a scalar conservative energy. The target specializes to acyclic feedforward W and adds a least-action interpretation and finite discrete trace, so its novelty must be separated from the broader augmented-state exact-gradient construction.

competitive_landscape.title: Equilibrium Propagation with Continual Weight Updates
competitive_landscape.difference: Continual Equilibrium Propagation interleaves neural relaxation and local weight updates, reducing phase separation but using a small-learning-rate approximation to the equilibrium gradient. The target holds parameters fixed during state relaxation and proves exact feedforward gradients, while offering no continual synaptic-update experiment.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
competitive_landscape.difference: Neural ODEs train continuous-depth dynamics with an adjoint integrated backward in time and trade activation storage for recomputation. The target instead relaxes an acyclic finite network toward a fixed point and carries stress in the same forward time coordinate, but its equation still implements the transposed Jacobian action central to an adjoint.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims that exact backpropagation is the natural equilibrium and finite discrete trace of a dissipative doubled least-action system, unifying inference and credit assignment without an explicit backward phase and suggesting a route to physical learning hardware.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The mean-stress algebra, nilpotent finite Neumann series, forward-freezing proof, and 2L unit-step recurrence establish an exact re-expression of feedforward BP. A CIFAR-10 run shows near-autograd directions and accuracy across four relaxation step sizes.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Exact local/relaxation alternatives, doubled-state schemes, adjoints, and equilibrium physical learning all predate this work. The credible novelty is the particular Bateman-Galley/Rayleigh formulation and its transparent nilpotent 2L trace. It is not yet a distinct efficient learning algorithm or a removal of reverse transport: W^T remains explicit, dissipation is added beyond stationary action, continuous finite-time and global-stability language overreach the proofs, and the only empirical validation shows expected parity without a cost or hardware advantage.

reviewer_notes: The index-pinned 22-page extraction was read end to end, including the full main text, references, every equation and table, and every appendix A-H: out-of-equilibrium/Bateman-Galley mechanics and Lagrangian construction (A), inertial second-order extension (B), complete relaxation algorithm (C), forward-freezing proof (D), discrete algorithm (E), equilibrium equivalence and stability argument (F), approximate split dynamics (G), and all training, norm, cosine, SNR, and layerwise-error figures (H, through page 22). The artifact is the current arXiv:2602.02281v2 PDF, whose displayed v2 title is 'A Physical Theory of Backpropagation: Exact Gradients from the Least-Action Principle'; a fresh primary-source download checked 2026-08-23 matched indexed PDF SHA-256 af54cb8d4629c3e54f1add4d0696ec1366101b96fafdc0968ce10ae0525be0ce, and the cached extraction matched text SHA-256 23c72ad6a9db35afbefb9a87d58efb37c85849a411b1718122b3e63395466946 with 22/22 text-bearing pages. Six direct primary-source competitors were checked at the exact arXiv versions recorded above on 2026-08-23. Author-stated limitations, reviewer-identified limitations, negative evidence, and internal contradictions are labeled separately. The central synthesis guardrail is that the paper proves an exact algebraic re-scheduling of BP under restrictive feedforward assumptions; it does not show that least action alone creates the relaxation, eliminate W^T, prove global nonlinear stability, or establish a physical/computational efficiency gain.
